criteria: A required argument, parameter, field, property or option was not supplied at all by the caller. Use when the key is absent; if it was supplied but empty use empty-required-field, if supplied as null use null-argument, if it is a configuration key use missing-required-config.
A required value was supplied but carries nothing — empty string, empty list, empty object, whitespace only. The key is present, the content is not.
An argument was passed as null, nil, undefined, None or a zero pointer where the callee requires a value, including null members inside a supplied collection.
An argument of an acceptable type carries content the callee refuses after checking it, and no more specific family applies. The general fallback for argument validation.
A string argument does not match the syntax the callee parses, and no format-specific family fits (see invalid-url-format, invalid-date-format, invalid-regex-pattern, invalid-identifier-format).
The number of arguments is wrong: too few, too many, or a variadic call whose count does not match a format string, signature or arity check. About how many, not about what they contain.

A numeric or sized value is outside the accepted bounds — negative where positive is required, over a maximum, under a minimum, a bad percentage, a port outside 1-65535. Not for indexing past the end of a collection (index-out-of-range).
The value is outside a fixed set of names the callee defines — a mode, strategy, driver, algorithm, log level or other closed option set. The message usually lists the accepted names.
Two or more supplied options, flags, arguments or config keys cannot be used together, or one of them requires a companion that is absent. The fault is the combination, not any single value.
A name, key, identifier, slug or label breaks the rules for identifiers here: reserved word, forbidden characters, wrong length, wrong prefix or casing.

A name, key or id is already taken in a registry, map, namespace or plugin table, so the second registration is refused. Not for a stored entity that already exists (resource-already-exists) or a file (file-already-exists).
An object, client or handle cannot be constructed because the arguments to its constructor or factory are unusable together — about building the instance, not calling a method on one.

A command-line invocation is missing a required flag, option, subcommand or positional argument, so the tool exits with usage. Use only when the surface is a CLI; the library-call equivalent is missing-required-argument.
A command-line flag, option or positional argument was supplied with a value the tool rejects, or an unknown flag was passed. Use only when the surface is a CLI.
A configuration file, block, key, field or credential the component needs is absent from the configuration it was given. About configuration, not about arguments to a call.

A single configuration value is present but unusable: wrong type, unsupported setting, or a value the loader validates and rejects. Two settings that contradict each other are mutually-exclusive-options.
The configuration contains a key the reader does not recognize — a typo or a setting from another version — and it refuses rather than ignores it.
A required environment variable is unset or empty at the point it is read.
An environment variable is set but its value cannot be used: unparseable, out of range, or not one of the accepted names.
The configuration file itself is missing at every path the loader searched. Not a missing key inside a file that was found (missing-required-config).
A configuration file was found but could not be parsed or loaded into settings — syntax error, wrong document shape, unsupported version of the format.

A document, payload or request was checked against a declared schema (JSON Schema, protobuf, OpenAPI, a validator library, a model's field rules) and failed it. The check is schema-driven, not a hand-written argument guard.

A value is the wrong type for where it is used — a string where a number is required, a list where an object is, a wrong class or interface, or input of a kind a documented API refuses. About the type, not about the content of a right-typed value.
An explicit cast, coercion or parse from one type to another failed on the value it was given: string to number, timestamp to date, bytes to string.

The kind of source, input or backend supplied is not one this operation handles at all — a directory where a file reader was invoked, a stream where a buffer is required, an unsupported input modality.
Text that was supposed to be JSON could not be parsed: truncated, trailing content, wrong quoting, HTML where JSON was expected. Covers decoding a JSON response body.
A value could not be encoded to JSON — circular reference, unsupported type, a marshaller refusing a field.
A binary wire format could not be decoded into a message: protobuf, msgpack, avro, gob, flatbuffers. Wrong field tags, truncated buffer, wrong message type.
A YAML document could not be parsed — indentation, duplicate keys, bad anchors, unexpected node type.
An XML or HTML document could not be parsed — malformed markup, unclosed tags, bad entities, wrong encoding declaration.
A template could not be compiled: unknown directive, unbalanced block, bad expression syntax. Not a template that compiled and then failed while rendering (template-render-failed).
A compiled template failed while executing — a missing variable, a function that threw, a value the template could not print.
A regular expression could not be compiled, or is rejected for unsupported syntax or catastrophic backtracking.
A glob, path pattern or selector expression could not be compiled or matched nothing legal.
A date or timestamp string does not match the expected layout, or names an impossible instant or timezone.
A duration, interval, timeout or cron-like schedule string could not be parsed into a span of time.
A version or version-range string is not valid semver or the scheme in use, so it cannot be compared or resolved.
Input ended in the middle of a structure the reader was consuming — truncated stream, partial frame, unterminated block.
A string contains an escape, encoding or code point the decoder rejects — bad percent-encoding, invalid UTF-8, unknown escape.
A URL or URI is unusable: malformed, missing scheme or host, relative where absolute is required, or carrying a scheme this client does not speak.
An IP address, CIDR block, host:port pair or network mask could not be parsed or is not routable here.

A remote service answered with an error status — any non-2xx, including a 4xx the caller provoked (400, 404 from an API, 405 method not allowed) and a 5xx from the server. The call completed; the answer was an error. Not rate limiting (rate-limit-exceeded) and not auth (authentication-required, permission-denied).
An outbound HTTP, RPC or SDK call never produced a response: transport error, TLS failure, aborted socket, client-side exception while sending. No status code was received.

A successful response arrived and parsed, but its content is not what the caller requires: a missing field, a null where an object was promised, a different schema version. The status was a success and the body was valid — an error status is http-error-response.
A call succeeded but came back with nothing — empty body, zero results where at least one is required, no content.
A service refused the call because a rate, request or usage limit was hit — 429, quota exhausted, too many concurrent calls. Retry timing is the fix.
An operation exceeded its deadline: a request timeout, a context deadline, a lock or wait that expired. Nothing answered in time.
A connection could not be established because nothing accepted it — refused, host unreachable, service not listening on that port.
An established connection died mid-flight — reset by peer, broken pipe, EOF on a live socket, stream closed under the reader.
A hostname could not be resolved to an address.
A socket, port or unix path could not be bound because something already holds it.
A request or response carries a media type, encoding or content type this endpoint does not accept or cannot decode.
A request or response body exceeds a protocol, server or client size limit. For a file on disk or an upload measured as a file, use file-size-limit-exceeded.
No credential was supplied at all where one is required — API key, token, password, certificate or profile absent from every source checked.
A credential was supplied and rejected as wrong: bad key, malformed token, wrong password, credential for another account or environment.
The caller is not authenticated for this operation — no session, signed out, login required before continuing. About identity, not about rights (permission-denied).

An authentication exchange ran and failed: OAuth token exchange, handshake, SSO callback, state or nonce mismatch. A flow completed unsuccessfully rather than a credential being absent or plainly wrong.
A token, session, lease or signed URL was valid but has expired and must be refreshed.
The identity is known but is not allowed to do this — insufficient scope, role or ACL, forbidden by policy. For the filesystem refusing on file mode use file-permission-denied.
A cryptographic signature, MAC or webhook signature did not verify against the payload and key.
Content did not match its expected hash, digest, size or integrity manifest — a corrupted or substituted artifact rather than a failed signature.
Data could not be decrypted or unsealed — wrong key, wrong algorithm, corrupt ciphertext, bad padding.
A TLS or PEM certificate, key or chain is unusable: malformed, expired, untrusted issuer, hostname mismatch, half of a cert/key pair missing.
A path, archive entry or URL was refused because it escapes the directory or origin it is confined to. A guard fired on purpose.
A file does not exist at the path given. For a missing directory use directory-not-found, for a missing configuration file use config-file-not-found.
A directory does not exist at the path given, or a parent in the path is absent.
The filesystem already holds a file or directory at the destination and the operation refuses to overwrite it. For a uniqueness conflict in a data store use resource-already-exists.

Acquiring a handle failed although the path was reachable: opening an archive, mapping a buffer, creating a temporary file, a sidecar or socket file that would not open. The failure is in the open itself; failing while reading bytes afterwards is file-read-failed.
Opening or reading a file failed for a reason other than absence or permissions — I/O error, unreadable device, decode failure while reading.
Writing, flushing or syncing a file failed for a reason other than permissions or a full disk.
A filesystem operation other than plain read or write failed: delete, rename, move, copy, stat, symlink, chmod, close.
Creating a directory or temporary working directory failed for a reason other than permissions.
The filesystem refused an operation on file mode or ownership — read, write, create or execute denied by the OS. For a service refusing on policy use permission-denied.
A path exists but is the wrong kind of node: a file where a directory is required, a directory where a file is, a broken symlink or special file.
A path string is unusable before any filesystem call: empty, too long, illegal characters, unresolvable relative path.
A file's format, extension or codec is not one this reader handles — wrong image type, unknown archive format, unsupported model or data file.
A file or upload is larger than the limit the code enforces. For an HTTP body over a protocol limit use payload-too-large.
The device has no space or inodes left for the write.

A named entity, record, row, key, session, model, plugin, table or object does not exist in the store or registry it was looked up in. The general lookup miss; use file-not-found for the filesystem and user-not-found for a user.
A user, account, member or principal could not be found by the id, email or handle given. Use this rather than resource-not-found whenever the missing entity is a person.
A DOM element, selector, UI node or accessibility target did not match anything on the page.
A query or search ran successfully and returned no rows where the caller requires at least one.
Creating an entity, row, account or object failed because one with that key already exists — a uniqueness conflict in a store.
An object cannot be changed, deleted or released because something still holds it — open handle, active lease, referenced row, busy device.
A cap on allocated resources was hit that is not about request rate: too many open files, connection pool exhausted, plan quota, max concurrent workers.
An allocation failed or a heap, buffer or GPU memory limit was reached.
The object or system is in a state where this call is not legal: used after close, started twice, read before initialization, wrong lifecycle phase. The call itself is supported, just not now.
Work stopped because it was cancelled or aborted — context cancelled, signal aborted, user interrupt, shutdown in progress. Not a timeout (request-timeout).
An assertion about the library's own state failed and the message says this should be unreachable or asks for a bug report. The caller did nothing wrong that the code can name.

The operation itself does not exist here: not implemented, abstract method not overridden, unsupported query operator, read-only implementation. Not a wrong-typed argument to an operation that does exist (type-mismatch), not a state (invalid-state-transition), not a licence or flag (feature-not-enabled), not an HTTP 405 from a server (http-error-response).
The capability exists but is switched off for this caller — feature flag, licence tier, build tag, experiment not enabled.
The call is refused or warned against because it is deprecated, removed or replaced by another API.
The operating system, architecture, runtime, browser or device does not support this code path or binary.
Two components, files, schemas or protocols carry versions that cannot work together, including a runtime or peer dependency below the required minimum.
A module, plugin, extension or native binding failed while loading or initializing, so nothing it provides is usable.
A required package, module, native library or binary is not installed, so the feature cannot run at all.
An optional extra is not installed and the message names the install command that would enable this path. The core library works without it.
A hook, injector or context consumer ran outside the provider, scope or request context that supplies its value.
An external executable could not be found on PATH or at the configured location.
A subprocess was started and failed — non-zero exit, killed by a signal, spawn error, unreadable output. Use git-command-failed when the tool is git.
A git operation failed: clone, fetch, checkout, merge, bad ref or object, authentication to a remote.
The working directory is not inside a git repository, or the repository is absent where the tool requires one.
A build output, bundle, generated file or compiled asset the runtime expects has not been produced.
A lock, channel or shared primitive is unusable because a holder panicked, a channel is closed, or a concurrent-access rule was broken.
A blocking wait was interrupted, or work was scheduled on the wrong thread, loop or executor.
Array, tensor, matrix or vector dimensions do not line up for the operation — wrong rank, non-broadcastable shapes, mismatched lengths between parallel sequences.
The element type of an array, tensor or column is not the one the operation requires, including a device or precision mismatch.
An index, slice, offset or key position falls outside the bounds of the collection, buffer or string being accessed.
An arithmetic result does not fit its type, or a numeric operation is undefined — overflow, underflow, division by zero, NaN where a finite value is required.
A read query failed at the database: syntax error, unknown column, planner or driver error while selecting.
An insert, update, delete, migration or transaction commit failed at the database. For a uniqueness conflict use resource-already-exists.
A connection to the database could not be opened or was lost — bad DSN, auth to the server, pool closed, server unreachable.
